summary: On April 27, 2024, Shower Pros LLC attempted to submit a quick payment using GovConnectIowa in the amount of $9,003.00 to be drawn from its bank account for the 2023 pass-through entity tax amount due.  When selecting to make its payment from its bank account on April 27, 2024, Shower Pros LLC was instructed to “Contact your bank to authorize payments originating from the Iowa Department of Revenue Bank Filter (Company-ID) 9426004574.”.  Upon successful submission of the request to have the payment drawn from its bank account on April 27, 2024, GovConnectIowa sent an email to Shower Pros LLC stating: “Your request has been successfully submitted.  On the telephone call with the Department, Shower Pros LLC was informed that the $9,003.00 payment had not processed, and Shower Pros LLC entered into a Tax Payment Agreement with the Department for $9,937.79 ($9,393.00 passthrough entity tax due on the return + $469.65 penalty for late payment + $75.14 interest due for late payment).  The $9,937.79 payment from Shower Pros LLC posted to Shower Pros LLC’s tax account on May 7, 2024.
title: Iowa Department of Revenue — SHOWER PROS LLC (O) 2026.
text:
ELECTRONICALLY FILED 2026 APR 13 11:04 AM ADMIN HEARING E-FILING SYSTEM
The appeal period has expired, pursuant to Iowa Admin. Code rule 701—7.19(8)(d) the Administrative Law
Judge’s proposed decision is final and the case is closed.
IN THE IOWA ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS DIVISION
CENTRAL PANEL BUREAU
IN THE MATTER OF Case No. 26IDR0001
IDR Docket No. 630741
Shower Pros, LLC
6123 W River Dr. PROPOSED DECISION GRANTING
Davenport, IA 52802, MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT
Pass-through entity tax.
On January 22, 2026, the Iowa Department of Revenue (“IDR”) filed a Motion for Summary
Judgment in the above-captioned case. Shower Pros, LLC (“Shower Pros”) never filed a resistance,
and a hearing was held on March 5, 2026, where two representatives of the business appeared as well
as a representative for IDR. The record was held open until March 20, 2026, to see if the parties could
resolve this case; however, this appears to have proven unsuccessful because the Tribunal was never
contacted. The matter is now fully submitted.
I.
The overarching issue in this case is whether IDR properly denied a request for a waiver of
penalty and interest related to a tax payment due in 2024, with the specific issue being whether Shower
Pros timely remitted certain business tax (with IDR’s computer system failing to take the money akin
to failing to timely cash a check sent to it) or whether Shower Pros failed to properly make available
the money. IDR’s position is more or less laid out in its well-support statement of undisputed material
facts, with read as follows:
1. On March 14, 2024, Shower Pros LLC filed its 2023 Iowa Partnership of Income
(IA 1065) making a pass-through entity tax election and reporting net Iowa pass-
through entity tax of $9,393.00. Iowa Department of Revenue’s Appendix of Evidence
(Dep’t App.) at 8, 32.1
2.No payment of pass-through entity tax was submitted with Shower Pros LLC’s 2023
Iowa Partnership Return of Income (IA 1065). Dep’t App. at 9, 32.
3. On April 27, 2024, Shower Pros LLC attempted to submit a quick payment using
GovConnectIowa in the amount of $9,003.00 to be drawn from its bank account for
the 2023 pass-through entity tax amount due. Dep’t App. at 10, 32.
4. When selecting to make its payment from its bank account on April 27, 2024,
Shower Pros LLC was instructed to “Contact your bank to authorize payments
originating from the Iowa Department of Revenue Bank Filter (Company-ID)
9426004574.” Dep’t App. at 11, 32, 35.
5. Upon successful submission of the request to have the payment drawn from its
bank account on April 27, 2024, GovConnectIowa sent an email to Shower Pros LLC
stating: “Your request has been successfully submitted. Once the payment has
processed, it will be posted to your tax account.” Dep’t App. at 12, 32, 36.

6. From April 27, 2024 to April 30, 2024, Shower Pros LLC did not contact its bank
to authorize payments originating from the Iowa Department of Revenue Bank Filter
(Company-ID) 9426004574. Dep’t App. at 13.
7. Shower Pros LLC’s payment request submitted on April 27, 2024, failed to process.
Dep’t App. at 14, 32.
8. Shower Pros LLC’s payment of Pass-Through Entity Tax was due on April 30, 2024.
Dep’t App. at 15, 32.
9. On May 1, 2024, Shower Pros LLC received an email from GovConnectIowa
stating: “Your payment of $9,003.00 has failed to process. Contact your financial
institution if you have questions regarding your unprocessed payment.” Dep’t App. at
16, 32, 37.
10. On May 2, 2024, Shower Pros LLC resubmitted the $9,003.00 GovConnectIowa
quick payment, received a confirmation email, and then called the Department to
verify processing of the payment. Dep’t App. at 17, 33, 38.
11. On the telephone call with the Department, Shower Pros LLC was informed that
the $9,003.00 payment had not processed, and Shower Pros LLC entered into a Tax
Payment Agreement with the Department for $9,937.79 ($9,393.00 passthrough entity
tax due on the return + $469.65 penalty for late payment + $75.14 interest due for late
payment). Dep’t App. at 18, 33, 39.
12. The Department received the $9,937.79 payment from Shower Pros LLC on May
2, 2024. Dep’t App. at 19, 33.
13. The $9,937.79 payment from Shower Pros LLC posted to Shower Pros LLC’s tax
account on May 7, 2024. Dep’t App. at 20, 33.
14. On May 2, 2024, Shower Pros LLC submitted a penalty waiver request listing the
reason for the request as: “Taxpayer is required to pay the tax by electronic funds
transfer, and the availability of funds is delayed due to reasons beyond the control of
the taxpayer.” Dep’t App. at 21, 33.
15. On July 3, 2024, the Department denied Shower Pros LLC’s penalty waiver
request. Dep’t App. at 22, 33, 40.
16. On August 24, 2024, Shower Pros LLC appealed the denial of its penalty waiver
request. Dep’t App. at 23, 33.
17. On informal review, the Department affirmed its denial of Shower Pros LLC’s
penalty waiver request. Dep’t App. at 33, 41-42.
Statement of Undisputed Material Fact, at pp. 1-2. Of note, IDR statements of material fact were
built in part on Shower Pros failure to respond to the request for admission that: “From April 27,
- 2 -

2024 to April 30, 2024, Shower Pros LLC did not contact its bank to authorize payments originating
from the Iowa Department of Revenue Bank Filter (Company-ID) 9426004574.” Appendix, at p. 13.
At the hearing on the Motion, the Tribunal inquired to Shower Pros about what happened
and why no response was filed, and Shower Pros essentially reiterated its claims from its appeal
request, which reads as follows:
4/27 I submitted both last year's and this year's tax payments for Shower Pros.
5/1 Just before 7 pm, Adam received an email that the payment failed to process.
5/2 First thing in the morning, I called our bank, they said they never received anything
or even denied anything and said there would be no issue on their end. I submitted
the payment again online. In the afternoon, Shower Pros called to make sure the
payment was received by the state. [D.M.] informed us that the second payment I
made that morning had already failed as well. She also informed us that the amount of
the payment was now higher because the state added a $469.65 late fee and $75.14
interest. She told us to fill out a payment waiver request and that is the only way to get
the late fee back after the fact. She ran another payment over the phone with us with
the new amount of $9,937.79. I called the bank again later that day to ensure they had
received the request for payment or even a prenotification. They did not receive
anything at all and verified again that all account information was correct. Since [the
individual] did not provide a confirmation or document showing she truly ran the
payment and I didn't see anything pending on the online portal, I attempted the new
amount again online one last time.
5/06 Talking to IHMVCU on the phone again they looked deeper and saw on 5/03
Iowa Department of Revenue sent a pre-notification to check status of account, the
bank responded with the green light but the state did not send the charge through. He
looked back to 4/27 and there were no attempts made to take payment.
5/08 Called Department of Revenue first thing in the morning. [The individual]
informs us that we have a credit on the account and excitedly says we will be getting a
huge return. I look on our bank statement and they started sending all four payment
attempts through. (2 payments each for this year and last years) We ask her if she can
stop the attempts and she says no. So we said we will call the bank and stop payment.
Which we attempted immediately, while IHMVCU was in the process of blocking the
payments, they posted. So they reversed the ones that posted, and stopped further
payment attempts. He kept one payment duo so that we would not have an issue
proving we have tried to pay and the money is there. I asked him for documentation
proving that the state never attempted to take payment until it was considered late so
I can get the fee reversed. I also have documented my first payment attempt on 4/27
before deadline. At this point, taxes are paid but I need to work on getting fee
refunded. As you can see from all the documentation I submitted with waiver request,
payment was attempted on time and we were falsely informed multiple times that the
payments had failed.
- 3 -

Tax Appeal, at p. 1 (emphasis added). Of note, Shower Pros honed in on its claim at the hearing that
IDR failed to accept the available money, and as a result, it cannot be said to have paid the tax late or
otherwise be responsible for any penalty and interest.
When pressed, IDR indicated that, if Shower Pros could prove its claim that IDR failed to
take the available money, then there would likely be a mechanism for relief from the penalty and
interest at issue. IDR, however, expressed skepticism that Shower Pros could prove its claim because
it had already asked for proof in its discovery request and received nothing sufficient. IDR notes in
particular the lack of evidence by Shower Pros the bank actually acted as it claims to have done, stating
in passing it is unlikely this one disputed payment would have difficulty if there were a general system
error by IDR. Realizing that Shower Pros is a small business that may not have the resources to hire
legal counsel for this matter or experience in litigation, the parties agreed to stay the decision on
Motion for Summary Judgment while Shower Pros had an additional opportunity to present IDR with
proof of its claims. As the time for the parties working this matter out has now expired without any
apparent resolution, the Motion must be decided.
II.
A.
Summary judgment is available in revenue proceedings under similar circumstances to that allowed
in traditional civil litigation. 701 Iowa Administrative Code (“I.A.C.”) § 7.18(5)(g). Summary judgment is
properly granted there is no genuine issue as to any material fact and that the moving party is entitled to a
judgment as a matter of law. Id. § 7.18(5)(h)(4). It may be obtained “upon all or any part of a party’s claim
or defense.´ Id. § 7.17(5)(g)(1). The purpose of summary judgment is to avoid useless trials or hearings
when the case can be decided as a legal matter. Sorenson v. Shaklee Corp., 461 N.W.2d 324, 326 (Iowa
1990).
“When a motion for summary judgment is made and supported . . ., an adverse party may not rest
upon the mere allegations or denials of the party’s pleading, but the party’s response must set forth specific
facts, by affidavits or as otherwise provided in this rule, showing that there is a genuine issue for hearing.”
441 I.A.C. § 7.18(5)(h)(4). Evidence is viewed in the light most favorable to the nonmoving party, and any
legitimate inference the evidence bears in favor of the non-moving party can establish a genuine issue of
material fact. Banwart v. 50th St. Sports, L.L.C., 910 N.W.2d 540, 545 (Iowa 2018). A factual issue is
material if “the dispute is over facts that might affect the outcome of the suit.” Phillips v. Covenant Clinic,
625 N.W.2d 714, 717 (Iowa 2001) (internal quotation marks omitted).
The relevant law here concerns penalty and interest for untimely paid taxes, and the governing law
on the penalty states in part:
If a person fails to pay the tax due on or before the due date, there shall be added to the
tax remaining unpaid by the due date a penalty of five percent of the unpaid tax. The
penalty shall be in addition to any other penalty provided by law. The penalty, if assessed,
shall be waived by the department upon a showing by the taxpayer of any of the following
conditions:
. . .
a. Any reason listed under subsection 1, paragraph “d”, except subsection 1, paragraph “d”,
subparagraph (11).
- 4 -

Iowa Code. § 421.27(2)(a). The referenced subsection 1, paragraph D states in part:
(1) An amount of tax greater than zero is due and at least ninety percent of the tax due has
been paid by the due date of the tax.
(2) (a) A taxpayer who is required to file a monthly or quarterly return may have one late
return or one late payment within a three-year period.
(b) If the taxpayer receives a waiver of a penalty under this subparagraph, the taxpayer
must make timely filings and payments for three years prior to being eligible for receiving
another waiver under this subparagraph. If the taxpayer receives a waiver under this
subparagraph, the waiver shall apply to penalties assessed under this subsection and
subsection 2.
(c) The use of any other penalty exception shall not count as a late return or late payment
for purposes of receiving a waiver by the taxpayer under this subparagraph.
(3) The death of a taxpayer, death of a member of the immediate family of the taxpayer,
or death of the person directly responsible for filing the return and paying the tax, when
the death interferes with timely filing of a return or timely payment of tax.
(4) The onset of serious, long-term illness or hospitalization of the taxpayer, of a member
of the immediate family of the taxpayer, or of the person directly responsible for filing the
return and paying the tax when such illness or hospitalization interferes with the timely
filing of a return or timely payment of tax.
(5) Destruction of records by fire, flood, or other act of God when the destruction
interferes with the timely filing of a return or timely payment of tax.
(6) The taxpayer presents proof that the taxpayer relied upon applicable, documented,
written advice specifically made to the taxpayer, to the taxpayer's preparer, or to an
association representative of the taxpayer from the department, state department of
transportation, county treasurer, or federal internal revenue service, whichever is
appropriate, that the reliance was the direct cause of the failure to file or failure to pay, and
that the advice has not been superseded by a court decision, ruling by a quasi-judicial body,
or the adoption, amendment, or repeal of a rule or law.
(7) Reliance upon results in a previous audit was a direct cause for the failure to file or the
failure to pay where the previous audit expressly and clearly addressed the issue and the
previous audit results have not been superseded by a court decision, or the adoption,
amendment, or repeal of a rule or law.
(8) Under rules prescribed by the director, the taxpayer presents documented proof of
substantial authority to rely upon a particular position or upon proof that all facts and
circumstances are disclosed on a return.
(9) The return or payment is timely, but erroneously, mailed with adequate postage to the
internal revenue service, another state agency, or a local government agency and the
taxpayer provides proof of timely mailing with adequate postage.
(10) The tax has been paid by the wrong licensee and the payments were timely remitted
to the department for one or more tax periods prior to notification by the department.
. . .
(12) If the availability of funds in payment of tax required to be made through electronic funds transfer is
delayed and the delay of availability is due to reasons beyond the control of the taxpayer. “Electronic funds
transfer” means any transfer of funds, other than a transaction originated by check, draft, or similar paper
instrument, that is initiated through an electronic terminal telephone, computer, magnetic tape, or similar
- 5 -

device for the purpose of ordering, instructing, or authorizing a financial institution to debit or credit an
account.
(13) For a death occurring before January 1, 2025, that an Iowa inheritance tax return is
filed for an estate within the later of nine months from the date of death or sixty days from
the filing of a disclaimer by the beneficiary of the estate refusing to take the property or
right or interest in the property.
Id. § 421.27(1)(d)(emphasis added).
B.
In this case, IDR’s Motion for Summary Judgment is proper essentially because Shower Pros
has not created a genuine issue of material fact on who was responsible for the delayed payment in
the taxes. Indeed, by all accounts, Shower Pros owed taxes in 2024 and the money for such taxes was
not transferred on time, with the only issue being the reason the funds were not transferred. For its
part, Shower Pros in its appeal request explained how it believed it did everything necessary to make
the money available to IDR as it had in the past, including by contacting its bank to authorize an IDR
withdrawal. In response, IDR essentially argued Shower Pros failed to prove such, in part because
IDR requested evidence of this in its discovery requests (including in its request that Shower Pros
admit or deny it failed to properly authorize IDR withdrawals with its bank) and Shower Pros failed
to properly respond to its discovery requests (including by either denying or admitting the question
about contacting the bank which means such is now admitted as matter of law). See Iowa R. Civ. P.
1.510(2)(“The matter is admitted unless, within 30 days after service of the request, or within such
shorter or longer time as the court may on motion allow, the party to whom the request is directed
serves upon the party requesting the admission a written answer or objection[.]”).
On balance, IDR’s position is persuasive because, even if the product of lack of resource for
legal counsel or personal knowledge about the requirements of litigation, the failure to respond to
IDR’s request to admit Shower Pros failed to properly contact its bank to authorize IDR payments
means this issue is now decided against Shower Pros (at least where there was no other resistance with
a statement of disputed material facts that is properly supported). Due to this, Shower Pros cannot
create a genuine issue of material fact on any of the grounds for relief from the penalty, which then
forecloses any claim on interest. In short, even if Shower Pros is correct (as no computer system or
systems if free from glitches), it failed produce sufficient evidence to create a genuine issue of material
fact on whether IDR caused the failure. As such, the Motion is proper and must be GRANTED,
which ends this case.
III.
Based on the foregoing, the Tribunal GRANTS IDR’s Motion for Summary Judgment, which
results in its action in this case being AFFIRMED. IDR shall take all necessary action to enforce this
decision.
IT IS SO ORDERED.
